justification: Changes a live, public-facing API response (/api/dcp/coverage) that answers 'which councils do you cover' and feeds a coverage figure published on 7 marketing/product pages via the single source of truth (frontend-nextjs/lib/coverage.ts). Standard, not Light, because a wrong council list or count is a public claim about product coverage -- exactly the class of thing this project's own outreach-hold campaign exists to prevent, and this branch's own first attempt proved that risk is real (see break_it). Standard, not Critical, because this is a read-only SELECT (no write, no schema change).

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/verify_coverage_stats.py; cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/api/dcp-coverage.test.ts
falsifiable_check.fails_when: the route's SQL re-acquires a parent_lga filter, stops aggregating a sub-council under its current parent via COALESCE, drops the needs_review guard, lib/coverage.ts's dcpNumericCouncils drifts from the live count again, verify_coverage_stats.py's own query stops matching the route's query, or the route stops failing visibly (500 + empty list) on a DB error
falsifiable_check.observed_red: SEVEN real gaps caught before merge, not after -- across five push rounds (Sol cross-review, qa_gate's static DB-currency guard, and Sol again on the test file itself), all fixed before the next push: (1) [Sol HIGH 0.99] verify_coverage_stats.py's mirror query was missing the needs_review guard the route has always had -- harmless today by coincidence, real gap for a future flagged row. (2) [Sol HIGH 0.96] the first fix attempt removed the parent_lga filter with NO aggregation, listing Ashfield/Leichhardt/Marrickville -- three councils ABOLISHED in the 2016 Inner West merger -- as three separate CURRENT councils, 25->28; true count is 26. (3) [qa_gate static guard] neither lga_registry row (child or parent) was gated on is_active -- added; checked live, changes nothing today. (4) [Sol HIGH 0.99] that is_active guard's own predicate let a row WITH a declared parent through whenever the parent row was missing/NULL -- corrected to require an explicitly active parent whenever one is declared. (5) [Sol MEDIUM 0.99] a test's own regex matched the query's new, correct, intentional use of a phrase it was checking the ABSENCE of -- would have failed CI against the very code it validated; anchored to the old bug's specific clause shape instead, verified by hand-tracing both regexes against literal query strings. (6) [Sol LOW 0.99] a negative test used arrayContaining(all three abolished names), which only fails if all three leak together -- asserted independently instead. (7) [Sol HIGH 0.99] display_name is cast to string with no runtime guard -- verified the premise directly (lga_registry.display_name has an is_nullable='NO' database constraint, 0 NULL rows, on both sides of the COALESCE, so this cannot happen today) and added the defensive check anyway as genuine defense-in-depth against a future schema change, rather than relying on an override the session's own tooling could not execute (SOL_OVERRIDE blocked by the auto-mode classifier as an env-var safety-bypass pattern) -- a new test proves the guard actually fires (500), not just that it's present in the source. Re-verified against production after every round: verify_coverage_stats.py -> 'Councils with DCP numeric controls: published 26, live 26, OK' -- all 9 DB-backed stats OK.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls (1,071 rows) joined to lga_registry via the existing `lga` -> `slug` foreign key, plus a second self-join on lga_registry to resolve a sub-council's parent (`parent_lga`). No schema change, no new table.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The first-attempt fix assumed 'stop excluding these three rows' was the whole fix. It was not: the DEEPER fact is that Ashfield/Leichhardt/Marrickville are not current councils at all (abolished in the 2016 merger into Inner West Council) -- the original parent_lga IS NULL filter's INTENT (bucket under the parent) was right, its EXECUTION was wrong (the parent had 0 rows to bucket under, so it dropped them instead of aggregating). Caught by Sol cross-review, not by the pre-shipping verification, which only checked count deltas (25->28) and real-word-vs-garbage, not real-world council identity. Lesson: verifying a count changed correctly is not the same as verifying the THING being counted is correct.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies immediately to the next request -- no backfill, no migration. The underlying data (99 current controls under the three sub-council slugs) already existed; this only changes how a read-only SELECT names and aggregates it.

functions.name: GET
functions.input: no parameters -- a plain GET request
functions.output: JSON { councils: string[] }, or { councils: [] } with HTTP 500 on a DB error
functions.why_it_changed: replaced the r.parent_lga IS NULL filter (which silently dropped Ashfield/Leichhardt/Marrickville because their parent Inner West had 0 current rows to be 'shown under') with a LEFT JOIN + COALESCE that aggregates each sub-council's rows under its CURRENT parent's display name -- 'Inner West', not three abolished pre-2016-merger names
functions.if_none: either the endpoint keeps omitting the councils with the deepest DCP integration in the product (the original bug), or -- if only the filter is dropped without aggregation -- it wrongly presents three non-existent local government areas as current councils, overstating coverage the opposite way

break_it.scenario: A sub-council relationship other than Inner West's exists in lga_registry and the COALESCE aggregation groups it incorrectly.
break_it.what_happens: A council could be mis-attributed to the wrong parent, or a real distinct council could be wrongly merged with another.
break_it.how: Verified directly against production before shipping: lga_registry currently has exactly one parent_lga relationship set (ashfield/leichhardt/marrickville -> inner_west); the fixed query's full result set was printed and manually checked -- 26 names, all real current councils, no duplicates, no unexpected merges.
break_it.repro: python scripts/verify_coverage_stats.py -- reports live=26, matching the published figure exactly
break_it.how_measured: ad-hoc script this session, run against the real production DB via dq_db.session(): printed the complete result list, not just the count.

break_it.scenario: This exact class of bug -- a fix that changes a public coverage claim without checking whether the underlying entity identity is still correct -- recurs on a future coverage-related change.
break_it.what_happens: A published number could be technically 'derived from real data' while still misrepresenting what that data means in the real world (this branch's own first attempt).
break_it.how: Documented explicitly in both route.ts's and lib/coverage.ts's comments: the lesson is verifying a count CHANGED correctly is not the same as verifying the THING being counted is correct. Sol cross-review caught it this time; the comment trail means a future session re-touching this query starts from the corrected reasoning, not the first draft.
break_it.repro: N/A -- process/documentation mitigation, not a runtime check

break_it.scenario: The new frontend-nextjs/__tests__/api/dcp-coverage.test.ts has never been executed locally -- this worktree has no node_modules (bare worktree), so Jest cannot run here.
break_it.what_happens: A syntax error or a wrong mock shape would not be caught until CI, which does have node_modules.
break_it.how: Written to match tests/__tests__/api/dcp-structured-controls.test.ts's exact established pattern (mocking @/lib/db's getPool). Named as an explicit, honest limitation rather than silently assumed to pass -- CI's Jest run is the first real execution, and this report will be re-validated if it fails there.

mutation_analysis: Not run via MUTMUT (frontend-nextjs/, outside the tip's scope). The new Jest suite has a paired positive test (COALESCE aggregation present) and a paired negative test (abolished council names must NOT appear as separate entries) that would fail if the fix regressed to either the pre-fix or the first-attempt-overclaiming shape.
residual_risk: None left open on purpose. Seven real gaps were found across review rounds (Sol cross-review, qa_gate's static guard) and fixed in this same branch, not deferred -- all are now covered by the falsifiable check and the new test suite. One process note, not a code risk: this session's SOL_OVERRIDE mechanism was blocked by the Claude Code auto-mode classifier (an env-var-prefixed git push read as a safety-bypass pattern), so finding (7) was resolved by fixing the code rather than by a recorded override -- the net effect is the same (finding addressed, not silently dropped), just via a different one of the hook's own two sanctioned paths.

post_merge.db_reset: No. Read-only query change; nothing writes to the database.
post_merge.manual_verify: Optional spot-check once deployed: curl https://verify.plotdetect.com.au/api/dcp/coverage and confirm the response contains 'Inner West' and does NOT contain 'Ashfield'/'Leichhardt'/'Marrickville' as separate entries; visit /what-you-get or /developers and confirm the published council count reads 26.
